q: 1. Which of the following methods is not used for drawing elliptical curves?
explain: Ellipses are commonly constructed by the intersecting-arcs, concentric-circles, or oblong (rectangle) methods; there is no standard 'tangent method' for drawing an ellipse.

q: 2. In case of aligned method of dimensioning, they can be readable form .............
options: bottoms and right side of drawing sheet
bottoms and left side of drawing sheet
bottoms and top side of drawing sheet
explain: In the aligned system, dimensions are placed so they can be read from the bottom edge and the right-hand edge of the drawing sheet.

q: 3. To facilitate extension, entries in the table should begin form .............
explain: Tables designed for future additions are conventionally filled starting from the bottom row upward, leaving room to extend entries above as needed.

q: 4. In full sectional view, the object is imagined to be cut off .............
explain: A full section is obtained by passing a cutting plane completely through the object, conceptually removing (cutting away) one half of it to reveal the interior.

q: 5. The lines which are drawn to represent visible edges and surface boundaries of objects are called ............
explain: Visible edges are represented by continuous thick lines known as object lines, outlines, or principal lines.

q: 6. The unseen/inner edge of an object is represented by
explain: Similar to hidden lines, these are represented by short dashes (often referred to as 'dotted' in older textbooks).

q: 7. Dimension lines and projection line in the drawing are shown by .............
explain: As per drawing conventions, both dimension lines and projection (extension) lines are drawn as continuous thin lines, distinguishing them from thick outlines and dashed hidden lines.

q: 8. System of placing dimension on a drawing work is .............
explain: Dimensions can be placed using either the aligned system (figures aligned with the dimension line) or the unidirectional system (figures always read from the bottom); both are recognized methods.

q: 9. Hatching line is a line which makes an angle of 45 degree with
explain: Hatching (section lines) should be drawn at $45^{\circ}$ relative to the main boundaries or center lines of the object.

q: 10. Art of writing title, notes etc. on a drawing is called .............
explain: The skill/art of writing titles, notes, and dimensions on engineering drawings in a standardized, legible style is called lettering.

q: 11. Working drawing is prepared not for .............
explain: Working drawings are used to prepare bills of quantities, cost estimation, and construction layout on site, but they themselves are drawings, not written specifications (specifications are a separate document).

q: 12. The locus of a point lying on the circumference of the circle which rolls on a straight line is known as .............
explain: A cycloid is, by definition, the curve traced by a point on the circumference of a circle as it rolls without slipping along a straight line.

q: 13. The locus of a point is a ......... when it moves in a plane in such a way that its distance from a fixed line is always a constant.
explain: A point that maintains a constant perpendicular distance from a fixed line traces a straight line parallel to it.

q: 14. When two graphic entities are at a constant distance apart along the length, commonly referred to as .............
explain: Two entities maintaining a constant distance apart along their length are, by geometric definition, described as parallel to each other — hence 'parallelism.'

q: 15. CAD in engineering drawing represent for:
explain: CAD stands for Computer Aided Design.

q: 16. The regular polygon called nonagon has ....... members of equal sides:
explain: A nonagon is a nine-sided regular polygon, with nine equal sides.

q: 17. Name the curve traced out by a point moving in a place such that the difference between its distances from two fixed points is constant .............
explain: By definition, a hyperbola is the locus of points where the difference (not sum) of distances from two fixed foci remains constant.

q: 18. Dimension lines and projection lines are shown as .............
options: continuous thin lines with zig zag
explain: As per standard line conventions, both dimension lines and projection (extension) lines are drawn as continuous thin lines.

q: 19. The two recommended systems of placing the dimensions are .............
explain: The two standard, recommended methods for orienting and reading dimension figures on a drawing are the aligned system and the unidirectional system.

q: 20. Which of the following is the correct statement for dimensioning a view?
options: All of them should be placed within a view
All of them should be placed close to the parts being dimensioned
They should be marked from visible outlines rather than from hidden line
Dimensions indicated in one view may be repeated in another view
explain: Good dimensioning practice requires dimensions to be taken/marked from visible outlines rather than from hidden (dashed) lines, since hidden-line dimensions are less reliable and clear.

q: 21. The line connecting a view to note is called .............
explain: A leader line is a thin line (often ending in an arrowhead or dot) used to connect a note, label, or dimension to the specific feature it refers to on the drawing.

q: 22. Which type of line has precedence over all other types of lines?
explain: Per line-precedence conventions in drafting, a visible (continuous, outline) line always takes precedence over hidden lines and center lines when they coincide on a drawing.

q: 23. Which of following publications made by Bureau of Indian Standards includes standard techniques for line conventions and lettering in detail?
explain: SP 46 (Engineering Drawing Practice for Schools and Colleges), published by the Bureau of Indian Standards, is the comprehensive reference document detailing line conventions, lettering standards, and other drawing practices.

q: 24. Working drawing are also referred to as .............
explain: Working drawings, being the detailed drawings used directly for building/manufacturing, are also commonly referred to as construction drawings.

q: 25. Section lining is drawn with line at .............
explain: As per standard hatching conventions, section lining (hatching) is typically drawn at 45° to the main outline/axis of the sectioned part.

q: 26. The set of technical drawings used during the manufacturing phase of a product including civil construction are known as .............
explain: Working drawings are, by definition, the complete technical drawing set used during the actual manufacturing/construction phase of a product or building.

q: 27. Hatching line is a line which makes an angle of 45° with .............
explain: Standard hatching convention draws section lines at 45° to the main outline or principal axis of the sectioned component, rather than to a fixed horizontal/vertical reference.

q: 28. Which of the following curves obeys the Boyle's law?
explain: Boyle's Law (pressure × volume = constant, at constant temperature) describes an inverse relationship (PV=k), which graphically corresponds to a rectangular hyperbola.

q: 29. The representation of any matter by some sign or marks on the drawing is known as .............
explain: Standardized signs, symbols, or marks used to represent specific materials, features, or information on a drawing are collectively called conventions.
